resources.string: Cial.ai watches for one thing only: whether a text field is focused, so it can show its microphone bubble while you type in other apps. When you dictate and tap Insert, it places the finished text into that focused field. It does not read your messages, does not record in the background, and does not collect, store or share your text or audio. Audio is processed by your device speech service. Dictated text is sent only to the AI provider you choose in Settings, and only when you have added your own API key.
Step 1: Turn on the Cial.ai assistant
Cial.ai uses an Android Accessibility Service to notice when a text field is focused and to place finished text into it. Android asks you to switch this on yourself.
Off: enable Cial.ai in Accessibility Settings
The microphone is used only while you are dictating, after you tap the Cial.ai bubble.
Step 3 (optional): Add your AI key for polishing

Without a key, Cial.ai works as a plain dictation tool and inserts your words as spoken. With your own API key, it rewrites your dictation into clean, ready to send text. The key is stored only on this device and is sent only to the provider you pick.
1. Open any app and tap a text field. The Cial.ai microphone bubble appears.\n2. Tap the bubble and speak in your language.\n3. Check the text, tap Insert, and it lands in the field, ready to send.

Cial.ai uses the Accessibility Service only to detect text field focus, show its microphone bubble, and insert text you approved. It never reads your conversations, never records without your tap, and never collects, stores or shares your personal data. Speech is transcribed by the speech service built into your device. When you add an API key, your dictated text goes over HTTPS to the AI provider you selected, only to be rewritten.
Tap Done when you finish speaking
AI polish is off. Add your API key in Cial.ai Settings to get polished text. Your words are shown exactly as transcribed.
